new_candidates.body:
### Proposal

An option for the Newton backend (opt-in is fine) that keeps every environment at the origin in the physics model
and applies the `env_spacing` grid only where transforms leave physics for display:

1. build the physics worlds at the origin (identity transforms in the cloner);
2. report `scene.env_origins` as zero in the physics frame, so tasks that add `env_origins` stay correct;
3. add the grid offset in the scene data provider that feeds visualizers and renderers, and in the USD / Fabric
   write-back. Cameras placed in an environment would need the same offset.

Terrain tasks would keep today's behaviour.

### Motivation

Today the Newton cloner places every environment at its grid origin in the physics model
(`isaaclab_newton/cloner/newton_clone_utils.py`, `builder.replicate(..., xforms=...)` and
`builder.add_builder(..., xform=...)`). Body positions are float32 world coordinates. With 4096 environments at
`env_spacing=2.5` the outer ones sit at ±78.75 m, at 3.0 (the lift task) ±94.5 m, at 10.0 ±315 m. Between 64 and
128 m, neighbouring float32 values are 7.6 µm apart.

MuJoCo-Warp integrates `qpos += dt * qvel` in float32. Any motion slower than spacing / (2·dt) is rounded away, while
`qvel` keeps its value. At 64 to 128 m that is 3.8 mm/s at dt = 1 ms, and 0.46 mm/s at dt = 1/120 s. A smaller
step freezes faster motion. So the same environment behaves differently depending on where it sits in the grid:

- slow motion stops in the outer environments while the body still reports its velocity;
- contacts whose normal lies in the grid plane (any grasp, any push against a wall) settle at a different depth
  than at the origin and then stay frozen there;
- contacts with a vertical normal, like an object resting on a table, are not affected.

This matters most for fine contact work (micrometre penetrations, hydroelastic contacts, tactile sensing), which is
what we do.

Newton itself recommends the opposite placement. `ModelBuilder.replicate()`: "For visual separation of worlds, it is
recommended to use the viewer's `set_world_offsets()` method instead of physical spacing. This improves numerical
stability by keeping all worlds at the origin in the physics simulation."

Related issues:

- newton-physics/newton#5177: the float32 `qpos` freeze (open; the maintainers reproduced it and are discussing a
  fix in the integrator). This proposal is about where Isaac Lab puts the worlds, which removes the cause for grid
  environments whatever the integrator does.
- newton-physics/newton#32 and newton-physics/newton#947: world offsets moved from the state into the viewer.
- newton-physics/newton#5184 / newton-physics/newton#5185: contact writing far from the origin, fixed for Newton's
  own contacts, not for `use_mujoco_contacts`.
- #4175: set the Newton viewer's offsets to 0 because the worlds are already spaced in physics.

### Alternatives

- **`env_spacing=0` today.** It works for the physics: Newton worlds do not collide with each other (in our check,
  cubes dropped from different heights into the same place behave identically in every environment). The Newton GL
  visualizer can still spread the worlds out with `NewtonGLBackendCfg.world_spacing`. But everything that renders
  the shared stage breaks: the Kit viewport and RTX cameras show all environments on top of each other. It also
  does not apply to terrain-based origins.
- **A smaller `env_spacing` or fewer environments.** This only reduces the effect: at 10 m a body moving at 1 mm/s
  already loses 5 % of its travel, and a resting box sits 11 µm deeper.
- **Waiting for a fix in the integrator (newton-physics/newton#5177).** That would remove the freeze, but positions
  far from the origin would still have a coarser resolution than at the origin.

### Build Info

- Isaac Lab Version: 3.0.0-EA (run); `main` at `67fe128` (code reading: the cloner still places the worlds
  physically)
- Isaac Sim Version: 6.1.0

The Newton-only repro was run on Newton 1.6.1 and Newton `main` at `4ceba54`.

### Additional context

**Repro, Newton only** (attached `world_offset_repro.py`). One model with one world per offset, placed with
`replicate(..., xforms=...)` as the cloner does. dt = 1 ms, `SolverMuJoCo`. Scenes:

- a free body moving at 1 mm/s along the offset axis, no gravity;
- a 0.1 m, 1 kg box resting on a static plate, MuJoCo-Warp contacts (Isaac Lab's default);
- a 20 mm hydroelastic sphere resting on a hydroelastic plate.

"Along the normal" means the offset is along the contact normal, as for a grasp in an x-y grid. "In plane" means
the offset is perpendicular to it, as for an object on a table.

| offset m | float32 spacing µm | free body, moved in 1 s (expected 1.000 mm) | box, along the normal: depth µm | box, in plane: depth µm | sphere, along the normal: depth µm / contacts | sphere, in plane: depth µm / contacts |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | 1.000 | 17.12 | 17.12 | 183.98 / 96 | 183.98 / 96 |
| 1 | 0.119 | 0.954 | 18.53 | 17.12 | 182.64 / 96 | 183.98 / 96 |
| 10 | 0.954 | 0.954 | 28.42 | 17.12 | 186.69 / 96 | 184.01 / 96 |
| 79 | 7.63 | 0.000 | 141.91 | 17.12 | 402.22 / 200 | 184.01 / 96 |
| 315 | 30.5 | 0.000 | 12.21 | 17.12 | 203.86 / 112 | 184.01 / 96 |
| 1000 | 61 | 0.000 | 12.21 | 17.12 | 722.66 / 364 | 184.02 / 96 |

- **Frozen bodies.** In every world from 1 m out along the normal, the body takes a single position over the last
  0.5 s. It still reports a vertical velocity, up to 2.9 mm/s for the box at 79 m. The solver balances the weight
  with a velocity that the integrator rounds away.
- **Where the body stops depends on how it landed.** On Newton 1.6.1 the box sits at 103.76 / 195.31 µm at
  315 / 1000 m instead of 12.21.
- **Same picture on main.** Newton `main` (which has newton-physics/newton#5185) and 1.6.1 show the same pattern.
  Single frozen depths differ by about 1 µm or less below 100 m. So the integrator dominates, not the contact
  writing.

**The same inside Isaac Lab** (attached `isaaclab_spacing_check_v2.py`, v3.0.0-EA, Newton backend, 9
environments in a 3 × 3 grid, dt = 1 ms). Each environment has a cube without gravity moving at 1 mm/s along x:

- `env_spacing=100`: the cubes in the six environments at x = ±100 m move 0.000 mm in 1 s, while still
  reporting 1.000 mm/s. The three at x = 0 move 1.000 mm.
- `env_spacing=0`: all nine move 1.000 mm.

Resting cubes on the ground plane are not affected in either case (107.79 µm in every environment). The script
keeps the moving cube free of gravity with MuJoCo's `mjc:gravcomp = 1`, because `disable_gravity=True` is not
applied per body on the Newton backend (see its docstring; newton-physics/newton#5179).

**Open points.** Does this fit your plans for the Newton backend? The current docs point the other way ("set
`InteractiveSceneCfg.env_spacing` for world placement"). Is the scene data provider the right place for the
display offset? Newton's tiled camera already ray-traces each world separately, so Newton-rendered cameras should
not need the offset at all; we have not tested that.

We are happy to test a branch.

### Checklist

- [x] I have checked that there is no similar issue in the repo (**required**)

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With the option on, a grid scene on the Newton backend has all its physics worlds at the origin, and
      `scene.env_origins` is zero in the physics frame.
- [ ] `isaaclab_spacing_check_v2.py` at `env_spacing=100` with the option on: all nine cubes move 1.000 mm in 1 s.
- [ ] The Kit viewport, RTX cameras and the visualizers still show the environments on the `env_spacing` grid.
- [ ] With the option off, and for terrain-based origins, behaviour is unchanged.

### Reference files

- [isaaclab_spacing_check_v2.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34810683/isaaclab_spacing_check_v2.py)
- [isaaclab_spacing_check.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34810682/isaaclab_spacing_check.py)
- [output_isaaclab_v2.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34810684/output_isaaclab_v2.txt)
- [output.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34810685/output.txt)

new_candidates.body:
When controllers are loaded in a specific order using `spawner`, that order is initially preserved. After configuration, however, the controller list is rebuilt by iterating over `controller_chain_spec_`, an `std::unordered_map`. For controllers with no chain relationships, their final order is therefore unspecified and may differ from the load order.

It would be useful to preserve the requested load order for independent controllers while still applying chain constraints to controllers that are actually connected. Predictable controller ordering could help solve timing issues like the one described in [kuka-ros/kuka_drivers#7](https://github.com/kuka-ros/kuka_drivers/issues/7).
new_candidates.title: Preserve load order for controllers
